messages.text:
Hey folks. Roughly 15 hours of nonstop rig time overnight (Sept 9 12:30 to Sept 10 03:16 CEST), and the R29 through R31 batteries are all in. This is the consolidated readout, charts attached, full receipts in the repo at <https://github.com/jcartu/glm53-flash-field-lab/tree/master/results/r29>. Everything below is in-post, the repo is just the drawer.

### 1. R28.1 vs R29 Runtime Baseline

Standardized decode runtime is flat. ABBA order, two independent boots per image, TP4 / DCP1, no speculation. Mean changes across the six cells range from -0.39% to +0.20%. That is the run to run noise floor, so no regression, but no speedup either.

```
Cell (C, Ctx)    R28.1 Mean    R29 Mean    Change (%)    Repeats (R28.1 / R29)
C=1, ctx 0        175.12       175.18        +0.04%      [175.2, 175.0] / [175.0, 175.3]
C=1, ctx 32K      174.54       174.88        +0.19%      [174.5, 174.6] / [174.9, 174.9]
C=4, ctx 0        490.69       489.93        -0.15%      [489.0, 492.4] / [492.4, 487.4]
C=4, ctx 32K      490.61       491.41        +0.16%      [492.1, 489.1] / [491.9, 490.9]
C=8, ctx 0        786.51       783.46        -0.39%      [788.9, 784.1] / [780.8, 786.1]
C=8, ctx 32K      783.21       781.05        -0.28%      [783.7, 782.7] / [782.9, 779.2]
```

### 2. Checkpoint Quality: Published vs QAD2500 vs TVN1500

We ran the 52 functional synthetic tasks and 32 long context history tasks across the three checkpoints. Small bounded synthetic suite, not a general model ranking.

Strict format: 42/52 Published, 44/52 QAD-step2500, 38/52 TVN-step1500. Semantic correctness (computed assignments allowed in the sandbox, no oracle JSON picking): Published 52/52, QAD 52/52, TVN 50/50 of assessable tasks. The two remaining TVN tasks emitted multiple different JSON answers, and under the no-oracle rule we do not guess which block was intended, so they stay unassessable.

History tasks (ledger retrieval and visible-length control, prompt sizes up to 820K tokens): R28.1 Published 32/32, R29 Published 32/32, QAD 32/32, TVN 31/32. The single TVN miss, a 524K-token visible-length control, had its row pass/fail classification 100% correct, but it summed the score to 41 instead of 40, a plain off by one.

```
Checkpoint       Strict    Semantic      History     Notes
Published        42/52     52/52         32/32       Baseline target (R28.1 also 32/32)
QAD-step2500     44/52     52/52         32/32       Slightly cleaner format
TVN-step1500     38/52     50/52*        31/32       *2 unassessable under no-oracle JSON
                                                     524K miss is 41 vs 40 off-by-one
```

On the weights: the TVN1500 on disk is Luke's real drop. All 49/49 LFS files hash identical against the HF branch, and the tip commit on that branch only updates generation_config.json (temp 1.0, top_p 0.95 defaults). Weights unchanged, and every harness arm pins sampling explicitly, so the config-only commit does not touch any executed measurement.

### 3. Speculative Matrix (18 Configurations)

3 checkpoints × DCP{1,4} × {mtp0, mtp3, dflash2}, each at C1/C4/C8 × ctx {0, 32K}, 30 s cells, two warmed repeats per config. Same boot repeats, except published/DCP1/MTP0 which reuses the independent baseline boots. Descriptive means, not significance tested.

```
Mode              C1 ctx 0        C1 ctx 32K      C8 ctx 0        C8 ctx 32K
DCP1 MTP0         175.0-175.2     174.6-174.9     781-793         781-787
DCP1 MTP3         260-275         270-278         943-955         976-1007
DCP1 DFlash2      217-234         228-252         55-57           59-63
DCP4 MTP0         155.9-156.0     155.3-155.6     688-693         687-693
DCP4 MTP3         231-235         229-244         849-875         869-899
DCP4 DFlash2      195-203         199-207         57-58           62-64
```

(Ranges span the three checkpoints at each matched cell.)

- MTP0 is flat across checkpoints, all matched deltas within ±1.3%, most under 0.6%.
- MTP3 gives the clean win: ~260-275 tok/s at C1 (about 1.5x stock), up to ~1000 tok/s at C8 on DCP1. Acceptance sits ~49-51% with ~2.4-2.6 tokens emitted per verifier step, steady across checkpoints.
- DFlash2 is decent at C1/C4 but drops hard at C8 on every checkpoint to ~55-64 tok/s, and the engine itself slows with it: verifier steps go from ~210/s at C4 to ~18-20/s at C8, identical in both trials and on all three checkpoints, so it is deterministic and not a checkpoint problem. MTP3 at C8 is fine (~950-1000 tok/s). We chased it down and confirmed the cause: the matrix launcher pins CUDA graph capture sizes to max 32, and DFlash K7 pads the C8 verify batch to 8 x 8 = 64 tokens, over the ceiling, so those steps run without a captured graph. A matched A/B on published/DCP1 (same boot recipe, only capture sizes extended to 64) restored C8 to ~277 steps/s and ~687-720 tok/s, a 14x jump, while C4 stayed ~205 steps/s both ways. So it is a launcher config interaction, not a DFlash model defect, and the fix is one env line. Receipts: dflash2-c8-confirmation-summary.json and dflash2-c8-collapse-analysis.json in the execution receipts.
- Checkpoint deltas inside the speculative cells scatter from about -7% to +10% at C1, which for a 30 s warmed window reads as acceptance noise rather than a real QAD/TVN effect.

### 4. LMCache PR #64 Overlay

D-Rock's #64 overlay on R29 passed its qualification gates: 205 CPU tests passed (2 CUDA-only skipped), 4/4 native GPU metadata lifetime tests, 144/144 byte comparisons across 4 ranks through the real copier/SHM/RPC/native filesystem path, and RAM 16/16 cells valid.

One honest caveat on the RAM numbers. Client throughput looked up at C1 (+2.9% ctx0, +6.1% ctx32K), but engine verifier steps/s were identical on both images (~96/s at C1, ~340/s at C8). The whole client delta is draft acceptance luck, e.g. ~48% stock vs ~52% candidate on the +6% cell. So this is not a patch speedup, the patch is correctness/transport work, and the timing says the engine runs the same speed underneath.

```
Cell (C, Ctx)    Stock tok/s    PR64 tok/s    Delta       Stock vsteps/s    PR64 vsteps/s
C=1, ctx 0        231.5          238.2        +2.92%          95.8              96.0
C=1, ctx 32K      233.8          248.1        +6.13%          95.8              95.8
C=8, ctx 0        857.9          845.8        -1.41%          342.0             338.5
C=8, ctx 32K      863.8          882.6        +2.18%          340.0             340.5
```

### 5. Disk-Cache Pilot, Root Cause, R30 Transition

The disk lifecycle pilot stopped early at the cold gate because external_miss telemetry was unavailable. Root cause found in source: the shipped recurrent checkpoint connector returns (False, None) from request_finished, so it cannot produce the per-request cached_token_stats response, even though the scheduler does record recurrent imports in the external prefix cache counters. The observer now has a rule for that counter-delta path, and missing counters are never filled with zero.

Since R30 landed while we were debugging this, the remaining disk campaign moved to stock R30 vs stock R29 (the R29 negative control must still fail the exact payload dedup gate). No measured evidence is discarded, the completed overlay GPU-transport and RAM data above stays valid as supporting data.

```
R30 pinned image:    localinferencelab/vllm:jovian-judgement-community-20260909-r30
R30 manifest:        sha256:5f6fcbc681f20b7c052815ca17511d9fe789aea314a17723c202789dd7adc131
D-Rock PR64 overlay: ghcr.io/yatesdr/jovian-judgement-glm53-lmcache@sha256:509265489dec08e15aab4c4cc2b531cdc0688e12f84547c4cef7b4157cf36bb3
```

### 6. R30 Disk-Cache Campaign: Results

The follow-up disk battery ran tonight: stock R29 as negative control (dcp4/mtp3) plus all six R30 arms dcp{1,4} x {mtp0,mtp3,dflash2}, 39 lifecycle gates each, fresh bounded L2 namespaces.

```
Arm                Pass  Fail  Unavail   What failed
R29 ctrl DCP4 MTP3   31     4       4    replay/restart exact_payload_dedup +
                                        replay/restart no_new_unreferenced (expected)
R30 DCP1 MTP0        35     0       3    clean, both dedup gates pass
R30 DCP1 MTP3        35     0       3    clean, both dedup gates pass
R30 DCP1 DFlash2     35     0       3    clean, both dedup gates pass
R30 DCP4 MTP0        33     1       4    restart.correct_and_identical
R30 DCP4 MTP3        35     0       3    clean, both dedup gates pass
R30 DCP4 DFlash2     31     2       5    replay + restart .correct_and_identical
```

Dedup outcome is the headline: the R29 control fails exactly the four dedup/orphan gates it must fail, and every R30 arm passes both dedup gates with zero new unreferenced payloads. The observer fix also works, cold.external_miss now passes on all seven arms.

The three "unavailable" gates on every arm are harness observability limits, not engine failures, and we wrote them up separately:
- cancellation.server_abort_observed: the only abort series (request_success_total{abort}) never increments on client disconnect in this build, we verified the raw counter bodies
- cancellation.live_retrieve_observed_under_pressure: retrieve_leases is an instantaneous gauge and the retrieve happens during prefill, the status poll can't catch it, the real evidence is the +32768 external hit counter that did move
- evidence.all_rank_payload_byte_equality: OpenAI responses don't expose page bytes, byte equality is covered by the separate 144/144 GPU byte-evidence test

The DCP4 identity fails are neutral facts: same request bytes, same prompt tokens, full 32768-token external hit, the visible cache marker correct and byte-identical every time, but the generated token ids for the short reasoning preamble differ after cache restore/restart (first difference at token index 1). Temperature 0 and a pinned seed, so the gate demands exact identity and fails on reasoning drift. The follow-up ran right after (R29 dcp4-mtp0, R29 dcp4-dflash2, R30 dcp4-mtp0 repeat): all three pass both identity gates, classification **not_reproduced**, decisive. So the campaign's two DCP4 identity fails stay recorded as a one-off with receipts, not an R30 regression. Full detail in r30-dcp4-identity-analysis.json.

One more thing from tonight: the DFlash2 C8 slowdown from section 3 is now confirmed as the capture-size pin, not a model problem. Matched A/B, same boot recipe, only CUDAGRAPH_CAPTURE_SIZES extended to 64: C8 went from 18.9 to 278 verifier steps/s and from 53 to 687 tok/s (ctx0), while C4 was unchanged. One env line fixes it. Receipts: dflash2-c8-confirmation-summary.json.

And R31 already shipped while we ran that (pinned `localinferencelab/vllm:jovian-judgement-community-20260909-r31`, digest sha256:da7157d5649a85298635c44b03eeb127837448fa42a45388e48ad9de4a99ff39). Its dflash2 launcher now defaults capture sizes up to 256 including 64, so the C8 problem above is already gone on stock R31. LMCache moved to f868580a (includes the #66 restore admission fix), and the recurrent connector is byte-identical, so the cancellation telemetry gap persists there too.

R32 landed at 23:51 UTC too (pinned sha256:c9ad4a6ef4aa55232df9ed1a37e85d94eb8c7d5349561a6cbe828e72b61de83c). It is LMCache only, D-Rock's #65 so overlapping checkpoint stores wait for the writer instead of recomputing, vLLM commit unchanged from R31, so nothing above moves. Known limit in the bot post: MTP plus strict JSON schema plus LMCache can 500, issue #726. D-Rock gave R32 a clean bill of health.

### 7. NVIDIA's GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 Drop

NVIDIA published their own quant of 5.3 Flash this evening (<https://huggingface.co/nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4>, ModelOpt 0.47 PTQ, MIT, 33 shards ~204 GB). We pulled it and verified all 35 LFS files byte-identical against the HF tree, so it's staged on our disk as a candidate arm.

Layout vs Luke's published checkpoint, from the weight map and config:
- NVIDIA quantizes the dense MLP of layers 0-2 as NVFP4, Luke keeps those BF16
- The MTP predictor (layer 45) is plain BF16 in NVIDIA's, MXFP8 experts in Luke's
- Vision tower is identical in both: 347 BF16 tensors, unquantized, same tokenizer bytes

Two gotchas. Their chat template predates Luke's tool-result fix (#3), so a tool message with content=None renders the literal string None. And their config declares plain NVFP4, which makes our launcher's modelopt_mixed flag resolve to modelopt_fp4; the MTP layer inherits the quant config in code, so speculative arms need a boot test before we trust them. Text-only no-spec boots skip that layer entirely and look fine.

The comparison ran overnight on stock R31 (TP4/DCP1, no-spec, one boot per arm, same frozen suite: 52 functional tasks plus 9 known diagnostic profile prompts, plus 32 history tasks and the bench). Reported on the same basis as section 2, see r31-behavior-reconciliation.json:

```
Arm         Func strict   Func semantic   Diagnostic   History   C1 tok/s   C8 tok/s
nvidia         43/52         51/52           7/9        32/32     177.4      784.4
published      43/52         52/52           9/9        32/32     174.9      780.9
qad2500        44/52         51/52           7/9        32/32     174.9      783.0
```

So on this suite NVIDIA's quant and Luke's are within a task of each other on strict format and semantic, same 32/32 on history, same decode speed. Not the AA-LCR run Keith asked about, that one we have not done, but it is the only same rig same harness head to head of the two quants I know of.

Note published scores 42/52 strict on R29 versus 43/52 here. Same checkpoint, different image, T1 sampling, one boot each, so a one-task swing is run-to-run variance, not a regression claim in either direction.

All three booted clean (nvidia resolved to modelopt_fp4 with safetensors as predicted, zero weight-load warnings), sentinels and bench validity pass everywhere, and NVIDIA even leads decode by ~1.4% at C1, single boot, descriptive only. On the bounded suite NVIDIA lands slightly below published, same ballpark as QAD/TVN, not a ranking. Two sanity arms too: dflash2 on R31's default launcher did C8 at 282.9/285.6 verifier steps/s and 713/739 tok/s, so the capture-size fix is confirmed live on stock R31; and the R31 dcp4-mtp3 disk arm passed both dedup gates and both identity gates (35 pass, 0 fail, only the known 3 observability-unavailable gates).

All receipts, sha256s, the gate matrix and the consolidated results JSON are in the repo link above. Production is restored healthy after every run.
